title: Choose the visual world for the CRM
question: The roll assigned The Departure Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Departure Board
options.thesis: Every lead is a service on today's board: where it is going, when it is due, whether it is late.
options.viewport: One dense sorted field under a hall clock: three service tabs, then lead rows reading SOURCE, NAME, VALUE, STAGE, NEXT ACTION, DUE, with the DUE column carrying the only urgent colour.
options.risk: Becomes transit cosplay if the rows are not genuinely dense and genuinely sorted.

raised.raise: One hall light governs the entire board; no component carries its own shadow.
Urgency rides one continuous scale of weight and signal, never a zoo of coloured pills.
A single density control propagates across every view at once.
Services are separated by deep empty gaps rather than by rules and boxes.
State marks the row itself: the active lead is ringed, a handled one struck through in place.

options.label: The Bahi Khata
options.thesis: The studio's book: every lead is an entry, and nothing is ever deleted, only struck.
options.viewport: A ruled page of today's entries with running counts kept in the margin.
options.risk: Ruled paper fights dense data, and the world tips into nostalgia the moment the ruling is decorative.

options.label: Dark-first console
options.thesis: Persistent panels on graphite, seams one pixel wide, destructive actions left deliberately alone.
options.viewport: Tiled panels that persist while their contents change, the delete action isolated with nothing near it.
options.case: Highest product clarity of the hand and instantly legible to a developer, but it identifies with your profession rather than your commercial world.
options.risk: It is exactly the category's predictable opposite, so it reads as every other dark admin tool.

options.label: Darkroom safelight bay
options.thesis: Work moves through fixed stations under amber safelight, irreversible past marked points.
options.viewport: Stations in order, a print emerging in the tray as the timer runs.
options.case: Declined: a web studio does not identify with darkroom printing, and irreversible chemistry actively lies about leads, which move backwards all the time.
options.kept: Total environmental commitment: one light source governing everything.
options.risk: The metaphor misleads about what can be undone.

options.label: Cracktro scroller queue
options.thesis: Rank is depth: one bitmap face on an emissive void, nothing ever enclosed by a box.
options.viewport: Baselines running past both screen edges, layers drifting at different speeds behind the front plane.
options.case: Declined: demoscene nostalgia is not this audience, and banning enclosure destroys the tabular scanning a CRM lives on.
options.kept: Rank carried on one continuous scale instead of badges.
options.risk: Unreadable the moment the list passes a hundred rows.

options.label: Miura deployable sheet
options.thesis: A hand-sized packet opens in one pull into a rigid tessellated field.
options.viewport: A row unfolding in place into its full record along linked creases.
options.case: Declined: aerospace origami is nobody's daily world here, and a parallelogram grid fights dense tabular data.
options.kept: One control propagating across the entire field at once.
options.risk: Geometry that fights the data it carries.

options.label: Cloud quarry
options.thesis: Blocks of weather cut from cliffs and assembled into buildings that rain from their own walls.
options.viewport: Stacked blocks with deep blue voids opening between sections.
options.case: Declined: nothing about working a lead is quarrying, and the world carries no state vocabulary the product needs.
options.kept: Deep voids as the structural separator instead of borders.
options.risk: Pure decoration over an operational task.

options.label: Doujin event catalog
options.thesis: Thousands of stamp-sized cells in a numbered hall grid, marked up by hand in biro.
options.viewport: A packed thumbnail grid keyed to a folded hall map, forty cells ringed in pen.
options.case: Declined: Comiket catalogues are not this audience, though the grid-and-map-as-one-space idea nearly earns its place.
options.kept: State applied as a mark on the item itself, ringed or struck through.
options.risk: Hand-marked state is charming at forty items and unusable at four hundred.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What every CRM ships, executed impeccably: left icon rail, white ground, pastel kanban.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement you already expect, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from HubSpot or Pipedrive, by design.
